title.narrative: Hacia un futuro con igualdad, con mejores sistemas de protecci¿n social universal y de inclusi¿n laboral - IILA

description.narrative: Contract related to: Hacia un futuro con igualdad, con mejores sistemas de protecci¿n social universal y de inclusi¿n laboral - IILA - Peru is currently in crisis. In December 2022, President Castillo was confined and Vice President Boluarte swore to lead a technical, transitional government. The scenario led to nationwide protests and a national "state of emergency" was declared. New elections are to take place at the latest in April 2024. The protests reflect discontent with the political class, wide social inequalities, and the exclusion of a large part of the population from decision processes and access to social services.Peru counts with an updated National Policy for Development and Social Inclusion (PNDIS) and the ambitious development plan Vision 2050. But a national consensus on social protection, or a social pact, are yet to be built. The EU is a reference and privileged partner in this field. Based on relevant expertise, EU added value and potential impact, and its importance for sustainable development, the MIP 2021-2024 includes Human Development as priority area 2. It includes the sectors social protection and migration. The action consequently also promotes migrant regularization, inclusion of migrants into national social protection schemes and their labour market integration.The Overall Objective is to see Peru make progress towards a universal, inclusive Social Protection System (SPS), with equal opportunities for all, regardless of nationality.Specific objectives (Outcomes) are:-To design and enforce legal and policy frameworks for a) non-contributory and contributory social protection and b) employment policies with a right based, intercultural and gender focus,-To increase the coverage, enhance the adequacy and improve the quality of social protection programmes and schemes and active labour market services at territorial level, with a clear focus on gender equality and interculturality,-To improve social protection and social-economic integration measures for migrants and refugees.The 19 MEUR Action (14 MEUR EU and 4 MEUR DE) shall be implemented by IILA and GIZ. It is complementary to bilateral health sector and migration support, and the regional TEI Inclusive Societies.

title.narrative: Proportion of population covered by social protection floors/systems

description.narrative: Disaggregated by sex, distinguishing children, unemployed persons, older persons, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, newborns, workinjury victims and the poor and the vulnerable. As of October 2021, SDG indicator 1.3.1 is a Tier II indicator please check data availability for your country of interest before selecting this indicator. If SDG data is not publicly available, baseline and endline surveys would need to be conducted and budgeted by the EUfunded intervention.This aggregate indicator reflects the percentage of the population covered by social protection floors/systems disaggregated by sex, and distinguishing children, unemployed, old age, people with disabilities, pregnant women/newborns, work injury victims, poor and vulnerable It also reflects the main components of social protection: child and maternity benefits, support for persons without a job, persons with disabilities, victims of work injuries and older persons. It is calculated as the proportion of the total population receiving cash benefits under at least one of the contingencies (contributory or noncontributory benefit) or actively contributing to at least one social security scheme. Calculations include separate indicators in order to distinguish effective coverage for children, unemployed persons, older persons and persons with disabilities, mothers with newborns, workers protected in case of work injury, and the poor and the vulnerable. Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg. Users are not expected to encode values for these indicators.For methodology, see SDG metadata repository at https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata/

title.narrative: World Bank Gini index

description.narrative: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income (or, in some cases, consumption expenditure) among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. A Lorenz curve plots the cumulative percentages of total income received against the cumulative number of recipients, starting with the poorest individual or household. The Gini index measures the area between the Lorenz curve and a hypothetical line of absolute equality, expressed as a percentage of the maximum area under the line. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality.

title.narrative: World Bank Gini index

description.narrative: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income (or, in some cases, consumption expenditure) among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. A Lorenz curve plots the cumulative percentages of total income received against the cumulative number of recipients, starting with the poorest individual or household. The Gini index measures the area between the Lorenz curve and a hypothetical line of absolute equality, expressed as a percentage of the maximum area under the line. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality.

comment.narrative: Throughout the 2000s Peru had been making gradual progress in reducing inequality through economic growth and increased public investment in social programs. From 2000 to 2019 Perus poverty rate dropped substantially and the Gini coefficient improved with supportive policies and programs targeting the poorest populations. However these gains were halted and even reversed by the COVID19 pandemic in 2020 as the crisis severely affected economic stability and amplified existing disparities.

The government of Peru has set a series of social and economic goals to reduce inequality in the country by 2050 in line with the Strategic Plan for National Development and the National Policy for Development and Social Inclusion. One of its key goals is to reduce the Gini index from 0.42 to 0.33 by 2050 which reflects an effort to reduce inequality in the country. According to the 2050 targets the country expects to bring the Gini index from 0.42 to 0.33 which would also imply significant progress by 2030 towards this longterm goal. The target for 2026 is 0.415 and for 2030 0.395.

description.narrative: The indicator proportion of the population below the international poverty line is defined as the percentage of the population living on less than $1.90 a day at 2011 international prices. Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg. Users are not expected to encode values for these indicators.For more information, see the SDG metadata at https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata/

comment.narrative: The projection of targets to 2026 has been made based on historical information from 2013 to 2022 published by the National Institute of Statistics and Informatics INEI. However considering that in 2020 the indicator has presented an atypical observation contrary to the results obtained up to 2019 it is not possible to make projections for more than 5 years since in order to do so more available information is needed therefore the MIDIS is committed to establish the projection of achievements 2030 2040 and 2050 progressively based on the results that are obtained and published.
